standards.name: MIRAGE (Minimum Information Required for A Glycomics Experiment)
standards.abstract: MIRAGE provides reporting guidance for glycomics experiments — studies that identify and characterize glycans and glycoconjugates (free or bound to proteins/lipids) from biological or synthetic samples. The guidelines cover experimental modalities commonly used in glycomics (mass spectrometry, liquid chromatography, glycan/lectin microarrays, NMR, capillary electrophoresis) and metadata describing sample origin, processing and definition. MIRAGE is coordinated by the Beilstein-Institut and the MIRAGE Commission (with academic contributors) and aims to improve the quality, reproducibility and reusability of glycomics data in publications and databases by specifying what metadata and methodological details should be reported and by recommending repositories and nomenclature.

classification.rationale: The source material is prose guidance and reporting recommendations (publication guidelines and checklists about what to report), not a literal rows/columns metadata table or an ordered workflow. Items are presented as recommendations/instructions to authors (what to include) rather than a field-level schema, so 'principle' best matches the document structure.

principles.principle: Provide detailed descriptions of assay conditions and experimental results.
principles.evidence: The primary aim of the MIRAGE project is to improve the quality of glycomics data in the scientific literature. Researchers seeking to understand the biochemical structure–function relationships of carbohydrates require detailed descriptions of the assay conditions and the experimental results.

principles.principle: Include a minimal set of metadata describing the sample's biological history, physical manipulation and chemical analysis so results can be interpreted, evaluated and reproduced.
principles.evidence: Failure to provide a minimal set of meta data describing sample’s biological history, physical manipulation and chemical analysis make it very difficult to interpret, evaluate and reproduce glycomics analyses that are disseminated as journal articles or database entries.

principles.principle: Use MIRAGE publication guidelines to report glycomics experiments (i.e., follow the group's publication guidance).
principles.evidence: The development of publication guidelines is the key task of the working group.

principles.principle: Report comprehensive sample-preparation information, including sample origin, processing steps (isolation, modification, purification) and a defined sample name.
principles.evidence: Following aspects are covered Sample Origin: General information, Biologically derived material, Chemically derived material, Description of starting material Sample processing: (1) isolation: enzymatic and/or chemical treatment; (2) modification: Enzymatic and/or chemical modifications; (3) purification: steps Defined sample: sample name

principles.principle: When preparing reporting checklists, include dataset-level metadata such as the data stamp, the responsible person and contact information, bibliographic reference and the date the checklist was completed.
principles.evidence: This is a general file that includes the data stamp when the work has been finalized, the responsible person and its contact information, the paper in which the data are published in a journal as well as the date when the checklist has been completed.

principles.principle: Apply modality-specific reporting guidance (MIRAGE has developed guidelines for MS, LC, microarrays, NMR and capillary electrophoresis — follow the corresponding guideline for each technique).
principles.evidence: Up to now, the group has developed guidelines for sample preparations, mass spectrometric analysis, glycan microarray analysis, liquid chromatography analysis, NMR glycan recognition and structures, and capillary electrophoresis analysis.

principles.principle: When publishing or depositing glycan data, refer to the recommended repositories and use agreed nomenclature (e.g., GlyTouCan registry and SNFG symbol nomenclature).
principles.evidence:
In order to promote these achievements, the MIRAGE Commission recommends the community to refer to these projects when glycan data are published and/or deposited.

GlyTouCan is a freely available, uncurated registry for glycan structures that assigns globally unique accession numbers to any glycan independent of the level of information provided by the experimental method used to identify the structure(s).

SNFG is proposed an universal symbol nomenclature for the graphical representation of glycan structures. The aim is to facilitate the standardization of how glycan structures are illustrated in publications.

standards.name: MIRAGE Sample Preparation Guidelines (v1.0)
standards.abstract: These guidelines cover metadata for sample preparation in glycomics experiments: samples are carbohydrates, polysaccharides, oligosaccharides or glycoconjugates derived from biological or chemical starting materials, prepared by isolation, enzymatic/chemical modification and purification, and recorded as named/defined final samples. The MIRAGE Sample Preparation Guidelines v1.0 were published by the MIRAGE initiative (Beilstein-Institut authorship) and published in Glycobiology (2016, doi:10.1093/glycob/cww082 / DOI package doi:10.3762/mirage.1). They are intended to standardize reporting of sample origin, processing (isolation, modification, purification) and defined sample nomenclature to improve transparency, reproducibility and consistency of glycomics datasets.

classification.rationale: The source is a prose reporting guideline containing instructions and checklists of what to describe (e.g. 'Describe how original starting sample material was generated...'), not a row/column metadata table or an ordered workflow DAG. Items are prescriptive reporting principles rather than discrete named data fields with concrete types.

principles.principle: Describe how original starting sample material was generated or where it was obtained.
principles.evidence:
Describe how original starting sample material was generated or
where it was obtained. Descriptions may include but are not limited
to material produced in the laboratory (e.g. chemically synthesized),
acquired from natural sources (e.g. human tissues) or purchased from
a commercial manufacturer. In the case of commercial material,
provide vendor and applicable item information. Starting material
descriptions are further delineated by biologically or chemically
derived material.

principles.principle: For biologically derived material, report cell type, growth/harvest conditions, modifications and species/tissue information.
principles.evidence:
Biologically derived material includes recombinantly expressed
proteins, cells, etc. as well as whole organisms or tissues.
For recombinantly produced material, the cell type (e.g. CHO, HEK,
NS0 etc.) and growth/harvest conditions should be specified. Any
modifications to cells that influence the characteristics of the starting
material (e.g. genetic manipulations) should also be stated.
For material isolated from tissues, the tissue type, treatments and/or
storage conditions should be reported. The species should also be
provided.

principles.principle: For chemically derived material, provide synthesis information or point to equivalent reaction protocols.
principles.evidence:
Describe how material was generated. If samples were synthetically
derived, provide information detailing synthesis steps or specify
where the equivalent reaction protocol is available.

principles.principle: Define the type of starting material that contains the oligosaccharide to be analyzed (nomenclature and sample type).
principles.evidence:
Define the type of starting material used or produced that contains
the oligosaccharide to be used/analysed in subsequent experiments.
These may include glycoprotein(s), proteoglycan, glycolipid, GPI-
anchored, free-oligosaccharides, sugar-nucleotides or synthetically
derived material but are not limited to these definitions.

principles.principle: Describe enzymes used for oligosaccharide removal or modification and provide source, expression/purification details and treatment conditions.
principles.evidence:
Describe any enzymes used to for the purpose of oligosaccharide
removal (e.g. PNGase F) or for modification of the starting material
(e.g. trypsin protease). Specify where it was obtained (vendor) or for
enzymes produced in-house, describe expression and purification
procedure. Also state if sample material was treated in-solution or
immobilized (SDS-PAGE, PVDF etc.) as well as temperature,
duration, volume, enzyme concentration.

principles.principle: Define chemical techniques for oligosaccharide release or other chemical modifications and report reaction conditions.
principles.evidence:
Define the technique for oligosaccharide release (hydrazinolysis, β-
elimination etc.) or other chemical modifications. Provide details of
reaction conditions (temperature, duration, volume and chemical
concentrations).

principles.principle: Document modifications applied to isolated material including type of modification, sources/kits, reaction conditions, workflows and enzyme details.
principles.evidence:
Describe any treatments made to the isolated material. Explain the
type of modification employed (e.g. hydrolysis, sample tagging
Chemical modifications (including fluorescent labels), isotopic labelling,
permethylation/peracetylation, etc.). Include source of materials,
description of kits used, reaction conditions and detailed workflow.
Document enzyme concentration, supplier, biological source,
incubation time and temperature. If novel glycosidase was used,
provide information indicating the origin (i.e. species) of the
enzyme.

principles.principle: Specify all purification steps used after isolation/modification and describe experimental materials and methods for each step.
principles.evidence:
Specify all steps used to purify starting material after
isolation/modification steps. Examples of procedures include solid
phase extraction (SPE), liquid-liquid extraction or other
chromatographic methods. For each method describe the all
experimental materials (e.g. stationary phase) and methods (e.g. flow
rates, fractionation etc.).

principles.principle: Provide a designation/name for the final sample following conventional nomenclature and specify the sample type to be analyzed.
principles.evidence:
Provide a designation for the final sample in accordance with conventional terminology. Resources
for glycoconjugate and oligosaccharide nomenclature are available in Essentials of Glycobiology
(Varki, A., Cummins, R., et al. 2009) and Essentials of Carbohydrate Chemistry and Biochemistry
(Lindhorst, T.K. 2003).
Name or specify the type of sample material to be analysed or used
in other experiments. These may include but are not limited to
Sample name glycoconjugates, glycosaminoglycans, N- or O-glycans,
glycopeptides, glycolipids, monosaccharides, poly- and
oligosaccharides

standards.notes: Source: MIRAGE Sample Preparation Guidelines Version 1.0 (18 Feb 2016), doi:10.3762/mirage.1; published in Glycobiology 2016 26(9):907-910. License: Creative Commons Attribution License.

standards.name: MIRAGE Mass Spectrometric Analysis Guidelines (glycomics & glycoproteomics) Version 1.0 (2025)
standards.abstract: These guidelines specify what information should be reported for mass spectrometry experiments in glycomics and glycoproteomics. The research objects are mass spectrometric experiments and derived data (raw MS files, peak lists, processed data, identification/search results) performed to characterize glycans and glycopeptides; the recorded modality is mass spectral data and associated files/metadata and search parameters. The document is an updated MIRAGE guideline (based on the 2013 MIRAGE MS Reporting Guidelines) published in 2025 (Lisacek et al.) and maintained by the MIRAGE community; it addresses reproducible reporting and data FAIRness by listing concrete metadata items to describe experimental design, raw and processed data location, raw-data processing, peak-list generation, search/identification parameters, databases, and search-space definitions. Scope covers items specific to glycomics and glycoproteomics mass-spectrometry reporting (data pointers, processing software and strategies, identification/search parameters, glycan database identifiers, fragmentation and tolerance settings, modifications and adducts, etc.).

classification.rationale: The source material is presented as a multi-column table with named metadata fields and an explicit 'Type of expected' for each field (e.g. 'Standard date ‘YYYY-MM-DD’ format', 'URL, dataset identifier/password or short free text', 'Number'), i.e. genuine field-level structure rather than prose checklist items.

data_stamp.evidence: Data stamp The date on which the work described was completed Standard date ‘YYYY-MM-DD’ format

responsible_person_or_role_and_contact_i.descr: The primary contact person's name for this data set with affiliation and contact information
responsible_person_or_role_and_contact_i.evidence: Responsible person or role and contact information The primary contact person's name for this data set with affiliation and contact information Short free text

location_of_raw_data.name: Location of raw data
location_of_raw_data.descr: If made available in a public repository, the corresponding URL, identifier/password or short free text, or if not public, name the contact person or source and internal coordinates of the data
location_of_raw_data.evidence: Location of raw data If made available in a public repository, the corresponding URL data set identifier/password or short free text or the information on how to retrieve the raw data. If not made available for public access, name the contact person or source and the internal coordinates of the data.

location_of_processed_data.descr: If applicable, URL or the information how to retrieve processed data (identifier/password or short free text)
location_of_processed_data.evidence: Location of processed data If applicable, URL or the information how to retrieve processed data. identifier/password or short free text

location_of_any_associated_data.evidence: Location of any associated data If complementary experiments were conducted in association with the present experiment, pointers to corresponding standard-compliant metadata unless otherwise accounted for in this report. URL, dataset identifier/password or short free text

ms_raw_data_processing_software.name: MS raw data processing software (name and version)
ms_raw_data_processing_software.descr: The name of the software and the version number; specify commercial or open-source and whether changes were made to original program code
ms_raw_data_processing_software.evidence: MS raw data processing software The name of the software and the version number. Possibly specify commercial source or if open source. If applicable, specify whether change(s) were made to the original program code that may affect the results. PubMed ID, URL or URI, or short free text

ms_raw_data_processing_strategy.name: MS raw data processing strategy
ms_raw_data_processing_strategy.descr: Type of raw data processing performed with the software (e.g. de-isotoping, charge deconvolution, peak picking) and parameters for generation/selection/smoothing of peaks
ms_raw_data_processing_strategy.evidence: MS raw data processing strategy Type of raw data processing performed with the software (e.g. de-isotoping, charge deconvolution, peak picking). If applicable, parameters for the generation/selection/smoothing of peaks. Short text with possible drop down list or PubMed ID, URL or URI

processed_data_file.name: Processed data file
processed_data_file.descr: Information about the processed MS data file including file format, availability, URI to access the file, scans combined and number of acquisitions used, and whether peak list was produced by summing or averaging
processed_data_file.evidence: Processed data file Information about the processed MS data file. This includes the file format and availability; if applicable the URI to access the file. Where available: - the reference numbers of all the scans (as numbered in the raw file) that were combined to produce a peak list, - the total number of acquisitions combined to produce the peak list, - whether the peak list was produced by summing or averaging the scans that are listed.

identification_software.name: Identification software (name and version)
identification_software.descr: The name of the software and the version number; specify commercial or open-source and whether changes were made to original program code
identification_software.evidence: Identification software (if applicable) The name of the software and the version number. Possibly specify commercial source or if open source. If applicable, specify whether change(s) were made to the original program code that may affect the results. PubMed ID, URL or URI, or short free text

identification_strategy.name: Identification/search strategy
identification_strategy.descr: Search strategy for precursor identification, including filtering, database or spectral library use, manual processing steps, spiked standards, scoring methods, etc.
identification_strategy.evidence: Identification strategy Search strategy for precursor identification, including if applicable, filtering of matches, use of database or spectral library, addition of manual pre- or post-search processing steps, inclusion of spiked synthetic glycans or glycopeptides, scoring methods for de-novo interpretation tools etc. Short free text

scoring_algorithm.name: Scoring algorithm
scoring_algorithm.descr: Method and software for scoring (for example, PSMs), along with the parameters supplied to the algorithm/method
scoring_algorithm.evidence: Scoring algorithm Method and software for scoring (for example, PSMs), along with the parameters supplied to the algorithm/method. Short free text, and PubMed ID, or URL or URI

taxonomy.name: Taxonomy
taxonomy.descr: Taxonomic details as an NCBI TaxID or TaxId; if not applicable, name of species as known by submitter
taxonomy.evidence: Taxonomy Taxonomic details as an NCBI TaxID or TaxId. If not applicable, name of species as known by submitter. short free text

glycoconjugate_search_space.name: Glycoconjugate search space (database and version)
glycoconjugate_search_space.descr: If database search, type and version of the queried database(s) and glycan search space; if databases not available online, content details to uniquely specify molecules and enable access
glycoconjugate_search_space.evidence: Glycoconjugate search space If database search, type and version of the queried database(s) and glycan search space. If the database(s) is/are not available online, content details, including any information that will uniquely specify molecules and enable access.

glycan_database_list.name: Glycan database list
glycan_database_list.descr: List of glycan compositions/structures and/or the glycan masses considered in the search. Expected accession number in specified GlyTouCan version for each, unless none was assigned
glycan_database_list.evidence: Glycan database List of glycan compositions/structures and/or the glycan masses considered in the search. Expected accession number in specified GlyTouCan version for each, unless none was assigned.

spectral_library.name: Spectral library
spectral_library.descr: If spectral library search, type and size of spectral library (e.g., in-house or public)
spectral_library.evidence: Spectral library If spectral library search, type and size of spectral library (e.g., in-house or public) Short free text

specified_protease_cleavage.name: Specified protease cleavage
specified_protease_cleavage.descr: In silico cleavage pattern available on the search engine as well as cleavage rules if they have been defined by the user. Note if software cleavage rules differ from the experimental procedure
specified_protease_cleavage.evidence: Specified protease cleavage In silico cleavage pattern available on the search engine as well as cleavage rules if they have been defined by the user. Note if the software cleavage rules differ from the experimental procedure Short free text

number_of_missed_protease_cleavages.name: Number of missed protease cleavages
number_of_missed_protease_cleavages.descr: Selected number of allowed missed protease cleavage sites
number_of_missed_protease_cleavages.evidence: Number of missed protease cleavages Selected number of allowed missed protease cleavage sites Number

additional_parameters_protease.name: Additional parameters related to protease cleavage
additional_parameters_protease.descr: If applicable, details of semi-specific protease cleavage(s)
additional_parameters_protease.evidence: Additional parameters If applicable, details of semi-specific protease cleavage(s) Short free text

amino_acid_modifications.name: Amino acid modifications
amino_acid_modifications.descr: Amino acid modifications (other than glycans) and their mode (fixed or variable) considered in the search. When applicable, specify custom modification and associated rules
amino_acid_modifications.evidence: Amino acid modifications Amino acid modifications (other than glycans) and their mode (fixed or variable) considered in the search. When applicable, specify custom modification and associated rules. Short text with possible drop down list

glycan_modifications.name: Glycan modifications
glycan_modifications.descr: Natural or induced glycan modification, e.g., permethylation, acetylation, reduction
glycan_modifications.evidence: Glycan modifications Natural or induced glycan modification, e.g., permethylation, acetylation, reduction. Short text with possible drop down list

allowed_adducts.name: Allowed adducts
allowed_adducts.descr: List of adducts that were allowed for the annotation (list of masses)
allowed_adducts.evidence: Allowed adducts List of adducts that were allowed for the annotation. List of masses

loss_and_gain_of_small_molecules.name: Loss and gain of small molecules
loss_and_gain_of_small_molecules.descr: Allowed loss and gain of small molecules, e.g. -CH2 for undermethylation, loss of water or sialic acids
loss_and_gain_of_small_molecules.evidence: Loss and gain of small molecules Allowed loss and gain of small molecules, e.g. -CH2 for undermethylation, loss of water or sialic acids Short text with possible drop down list

glycan_fragmentation.name: Glycan fragmentation
glycan_fragmentation.descr: List of allowed glycan fragmentation for the annotation run (A,B,C,X,Y,Z). This includes cross-ring and glycosidic cleavages
glycan_fragmentation.evidence: Glycan fragmentation List of allowed glycan fragmentation for the annotation run (A,B,C,X,Y,Z). This includes cross-ring and glycosidic cleavages.

precursor_and_fragment_ion_mass_toleranc.name: Precursor-ion and fragment-ion mass tolerance
precursor_and_fragment_ion_mass_toleranc.descr: For MS1 and MSn queries, the mass tolerance of precursor and fragment ions permitted by the search engine
precursor_and_fragment_ion_mass_toleranc.evidence: Precursor-ion and fragment-ion mass tolerance For MS1 and MSn queries, the mass tolerance of precursor and fragment ions permitted by the search engine. Number

thresholding_and_filtering.name: Thresholding and filtering
thresholding_and_filtering.descr: Other settings to the software that filtered out certain sequences from the database (e.g. allow only certain glycan types or restriction by composition) and usage of threshold for scoring values
thresholding_and_filtering.evidence: Thresholding and filtering Other settings to the software that filtered out certain sequences from the database (e.g. allow only certain glycan types (e.g., N-glycan) or restriction by composition). standards.notes: Field 'Type of expected' in source sometimes lists multiple acceptable representations (e.g., URL, dataset identifier/password, or short free text); where the source allowed alternatives the field type here reflects those options (e.g., 'url_or_free_text' or 'uri_or_free_text').

standards.name: MIRAGE Capillary Electrophoresis (CE) Guidelines
standards.abstract: These guidelines apply to capillary electrophoresis experiments used in glycomics and glycoproteomics, where separations (e.g. xCGE-LIF) produce electropherogram data files (.ab1 / .fsa) and derived ‘glycan fingerprints’ or glycoprofiles. The MIRAGE CE document (Version 1.0, 2021) is published as part of the MIRAGE initiative and in Glycobiology; it specifies what metadata should be reported for CE experiments (general features, sample identity and preparation, instrumentation and capillary details, analysis type and calibration, run processes and step-level descriptors) to ensure reproducibility and interpretability of CE-based glycoanalysis.

classification.rationale: The source organizes reporting requirements as named metadata items (Date stamp; Responsible person/role; Experiment type; Sample name(s) and descriptions; Sample solution; Instrumentation and software; Capillary properties; Type of analysis; Run descriptors; Step descriptors; Sample injection, etc.), each with concrete guidance on what to report—i.e. a table-like set of named fields with specific content and formats rather than only prose recommendations.

Date_stamp.name: Date stamp
Date_stamp.descr: Date on which the work described was initiated, in 'YYYY-MM-DD' format.
Date_stamp.evidence: The date on which the work described was initiated; given in the standard ‘YYYY-MM-DD’ format (with hyphens).

Responsible_person_role.name: Responsible person / role
Responsible_person_role.descr: Primary contact for the dataset, including affiliation and stable contact information (Name, Postal address, Email address, ORCID).
Responsible_person_role.evidence: The (stable) primary contact person for this data set; this could be the experimentalist, lab head, line manager, principal investigator etc. Where responsibility rests with an institutional role (e.g. one of a number of duty officers) rather than a single person, give the official name of the role rather than any one person. In all cases give affiliation and stable contact information, which consists of (i) Name, (ii) Postal address and (iii) Email address, (iv) ORCID.

Experiment_type.name: Experiment type (CE mode)
Experiment_type.descr: Mode of capillary electrophoresis used (CE modality).
Experiment_type.evidence: The CE mode (e.g. CZE , CGE, CEC, MEKC, CIEF, ITP, etc.), preconcentration (t-ITP), stacking.

Experiment_aim.name: Experiment aim
Experiment_aim.descr: Primary aim or type of glycoanalysis performed (e.g. glycofingerprinting, glycoprofiling, detailed glycan analysis, quantitation).
Experiment_aim.evidence: Glycofingerprinting (pattern comparison), identification (qualitative glycoprofiling), detailed glycan analysis, quantitation (quant. glycoprofiling), etc.

Sample_names_and_descriptions.name: Sample name(s) and descriptions
Sample_names_and_descriptions.descr: Name and concentration of samples, labels/tags used for detection, and identification of controls and calibrants.
Sample_names_and_descriptions.evidence: Name and concentration of sample(s) (if known) including any label, marker or tag applied that will be used for detection, such as fluorescent labels (by name only). Identify and give source to possible controls, system suitability standard, sample related standards/calibrants, tEOF-marker and test samples. If calibrants, state concentrations of materials (see section 4).

Sample_solution.name: Sample solution (components and metadata)
Sample_solution.descr: Composition of the sample solution excluding the sample itself: components, concentrations, pH, and manufacturer/order/lot numbers for reagents.
Sample_solution.evidence: The components, with concentrations and pH (excluding the sample itself) of the sample solution that is to be injected into the capillary including leading electrolyte (if used) and background electrolyte. Manufacturer, order and lot numbers used.

Sample_preparation_reference.name: Sample preparation (reference)
Sample_preparation_reference.descr: Reference to the MIRAGE Sample Preparation Guidelines or description of sample preparation parameters and history.
Sample_preparation_reference.evidence: Any general and specific parameters, settings, conditions important for tracing the sample preparation history as outlined in the MIRAGE Sample Preparation Guidelines (doi:10.3762/mirage.1).

Instrument_details.name: Instrumentation details
Instrument_details.descr: Manufacturer, model, catalogue number and component names (detector, interface) for the instrument(s) used.
Instrument_details.evidence: Manufacturer, model, catalogue number The name of the manufacturer for a combined unit or component. Type of sample-capillary interface, type of cooling (if any), type of detector(s).

Control_and_data_collection_software.name: Control and data collection software
Control_and_data_collection_software.descr: Name, version (or release date) and manufacturer of control and data collection software; detail user modifications.
Control_and_data_collection_software.evidence: Name, version (or release date) and manufacturer of the control and data collection software. User modifications should be detailed.

Capillary_purchase_or_source.name: Capillary (purchase/in-house) and source
Capillary_purchase_or_source.descr: If pre-made: model name, catalogue number, manufacturer and lot number. If in-house: supplier of manufacture/sources.
Capillary_purchase_or_source.type: object (pre_made:boolean, model_name, catalogue_number, manufacturer, lot_number, in_house_supplier)
Capillary_purchase_or_source.evidence: If the capillary was purchased pre-made (e.g. coated, with window, or pre-cut lengths) then include the model name, catalogue number, manufacturer and lot number. If the capillary has been manufactured ’in house’ then supplier of manufacture/sources should be given.

Capillary_material_and_properties.name: Capillary material / type / surface modifications
Capillary_material_and_properties.descr: For coated/gel-filled/packed/monolithic capillaries: manufacturer, catalogue number, lot number, type, surface modifications, particle and pore size, gels (as appropriate).
Capillary_material_and_properties.evidence: If using a coated, gel filled, packed or monolithic capillary, the manufacturer, catalogue number, lot number, type, surface modifications, particle and pore size, gels should be given as appropriate.

Capillary_setup.name: Capillary setup
Capillary_setup.descr: Single capillary or capillary array configuration (number of capillaries in parallel).
Capillary_setup.evidence: Single capillary setup or capillary array setup (e.g. 4, 16, 48 or 96 in parallel).

Capillary_dimensions.name: Capillary dimensions
Capillary_dimensions.descr: Exact dimensions: effective length (cm), total length (cm), inner and outer diameters (µm).
Capillary_dimensions.evidence: The exact dimensions of the capillary employed: from inlet to detection window (effective length, cm); from inlet to outlet (total length, cm); and the inner and outer diameters of the capillary (µm).

Conditioning_and_regeneration.name: Capillary conditioning/regeneration procedures
Conditioning_and_regeneration.descr: Flushing and conditioning procedures prior to use or for regeneration (including reagents, times, temperatures, frequencies).
Conditioning_and_regeneration.evidence: Flushing procedures prior to use. E.g. wash with 1M NaOH for 30 minutes followed by water for 10 minutes then BGE for 30 minutes at room temperature for conditioning /regeneration of an existing uncoated fused silica capillary or coating procedures, including frequency of refreshing coating for dynamic coatings. If an existing capillary is being regenerated, the capillary history should be considered.

Analysis_method_level.name: Analysis level / method
Analysis_method_level.descr: Specify method class: glycofingerprinting, glycoprofiling, or detailed glycoanalysis and associated validation requirements.
Analysis_method_level.evidence:
• Glycofingerprinting: Only pattern comparison, no peak/structure assignment.
• Glycoprofiling: Peak/structure assignment by database matching of normalized separation times without supporting exoglycosidase digestions (or complementary MS analysis). Reporting of all (potential) structures co-migrating within a specified separation time range is recommended.
• Detailed glycoanalysis: Validation of database matching via exoglycosidase sequencing or by MS. I.e., confirmation of assigned structures by sequential/parallel exoglycosidase digestion and or by complementary mass spectrometry analysis.

Calibration_and_normalization.name: Calibration / normalization
Calibration_and_normalization.descr: Describe whether and how calibration or normalization was performed (options include none, spiking, external/internal normalization, peak height/area calibration) and list standards/calibrants used.
Calibration_and_normalization.evidence:
• No calibration/normalization at all.
• Spiking for identification of single/individual peaks/structures.
• Internal or external separation time normalization:
External: pre- and/or post-run process(es)
Internal: in-run process
• Peak height/area calibration for absolute quantification by spiking in of quant. standards (calibrants) identical to sample components/constituents (in-run process). Name/type of standards/calibrants, if not already given under 2.

Run_process_sequence.name: Run processes (sequence)
Run_process_sequence.descr: Ordered steps for a run (preconditioning, preconditioning each analysis, injection, separation, post-conditioning) and specification of parameters across the run (voltages, pressures, polarity/direction).
Run_process_sequence.evidence: The protocol for a run normally follows the order (i) preconditioning prior to the first use of a capillary (various flush steps, designed to clean / activate / coat the inner walls of the capillary), (ii) preconditioning (carried on each analysis); (iii) injection; (iv) separation; (v) post-conditioning (again, various flush steps). Each of these steps needs to be defined as specified (Sections 5.2, 5.3 and 6, as applicable). There are also parameters that should be specified across the whole run (Section 5.1). Voltages and pressures should be described in terms of polarity (+ or -) and direction respectively.

standards.name: MIRAGE Glycan Microarray Analysis Guidelines
standards.abstract: These guidelines cover reporting of glycan microarray (glycan array) experiments in which a Glycan Binding Sample (proteins, organisms, aptamers, etc.) is applied to arrays of defined or undefined glycans printed onto a solid surface and detected by fluorescence/scan-based imaging. The MIRAGE Glycan Microarray Analysis Guidelines (Version 1.0, 22 June 2016; doi:10.3762/mirage.3) were published as part of the MIRAGE initiative to define minimal information required to generate interpretable glycan array data. The document defines eight areas in the glycan microarray workflow (Sample, Glycan Library, Printing Surface, Arrayer, Array Map/layout, Detector and Data Processing, Data Presentation, and Interpretation/Conclusions) and provides minimal reporting requirements for each. The guidelines emphasize retention of raw (Level 1) and quantified (Level 2) data while recommending presentation of processed (Level 3) data in publications, and are accompanied by supplementary templates and example supplementary documents to help researchers report experiments consistently.

classification.rationale: The source is primarily a prose guidance document and checklist describing minimal information to report across eight numbered workflow areas. Although templates are provided separately, the core MIRAGE document presents instructive items and reporting requirements rather than a single, self-contained field-level metadata table or an ordered procedural DAG.

principles.principle: Report an appropriate name, references, public database identifiers, origin and source of the Glycan Binding Sample.
principles.evidence: The Sample description should include an appropriate name, previous references, public database IDs (if available), its origin (synthetic, natural, or recombinant), and its source including vendor or method of preparation.

principles.principle: For organisms used as samples, include the protocol for propagation.
principles.evidence: For organisms, the protocol for propagation should be included.

principles.principle: For protein samples, state sample purity (quantitative or qualitative) and describe fusion constructs or tags used.
principles.evidence: For proteins, a statement of purity is required and may represent a quantitative or qualitative description; i.e., % purity based on a specific assay (quantitative) or a component of a mixture such as a polyclonal antibody in a serum sample (qualitative). Fusion constructs for recombinant proteins for the purpose of detecting should also be described.

principles.principle: Describe any direct labeling of the sample and list labeling methods and reagents.
principles.evidence: If sample is directly labelled, describe the method and reagents

principles.principle: Provide the assay protocol including sample concentration, composition of solutions, times and temperatures for blocking, binding and washing, and details of secondary reagents or pre-complexing (ratios, times, temperatures).
principles.evidence: The protocol used for microarray binding analysis of Sample should include Sample concentration. Describe the composition of solutions, time and temperature used for blocking (preventing non-specific binding) binding, and washing, as well as application of secondary reagent(s) required for the analyses. If the Sample is precomplexed with secondary detection reagents prior to adding to the array (e.g. anti-His antibody with his-tagged Sample) give the ratio of reactants and pre-complexing time and temperature.

principles.principle: Provide, where possible, sequence/linkage/anomeric configuration for mono- and oligosaccharide glycans and state the nomenclature used; include accession numbers from authoritative registries (e.g. GlyTouCan) when available.
principles.evidence: For mono- and oligosaccharides, the structure of each glycan, i.e. the sequence, linkage and anomeric configuration of each monosaccharide should be indicated using an appropriate nomenclature, which may be textual or symbolic as in SNFG (doi: 10.1093/glycob/cwv091). When possible, accession numbers assigned by an authoritative informatics resource, such as the GlyTouCan glycan structure registry (https://glytoucan.org/) should be included.

principles.principle: Report glycan source, purification scheme and an indication of purity (e.g. HPLC or MS profile) for printed glycan targets or fractions; reference MIRAGE Sample Preparations or MS Guidelines where appropriate.
principles.evidence: The purity of each glycan should be indicated [MIRAGE Sample Preparations Guidelines (doi:10.3762/mirage.1) are recommended]. Sources/references of glycans should be specified. ... Some indication of purity should be included; i.e., HPLC or MS profile of each printed glycan target or glycan fraction should be provided [for MS data, MIRAGE MS Guidelines (doi:10.3762/mirage.2) are recommended].

principles.principle: Describe methods/references for functionalization or derivatization of glycans, including linker structures and any effects of modifications on glycan structure; indicate purity of derivatives.
principles.evidence: Methods/references for functionalization or derivatization of glycans, including the structures of linkers should be described. Any effects on the glycan structure; i.e., reductive amination of reducing monosaccharide, should be indicated. The purity of each glycan derivative should be indicated.

principles.principle: Describe the printing surface (type, e.g. glass slide or microtiter plate), manufacturer or vendor product name, and any custom preparation/coating and the protocol used prior to deposition.
principles.evidence: As the utility of the data generated from a glycan array analysis will be related to the quality of the printed array, minimal information regarding a surface on which the array is printed should include: What type of surface is being used; i.e., microscope-glass slide, microtiter plate or other format. Manufacturer: Provide the name of the manufacturer or name provided by the vendor with appropriate description of the product. If the slides were custom prepared/coated, indicate the initial source and description of the starting surface; i.e., glass material, microtiter plate, etc., and the protocol used to prepare the surface prior to sample deposition.

principles.principle: Report immobilization chemistry and handling required for printed glycans (non-covalent and covalent methods, carrier reagents, linker chemistries).
principles.evidence: Immobilization of glycans may be accomplished by a variety of non-covalent and covalent mechanisms depending on the nature of the linker between glycan and surface of substrate. Describe the non-covalent immobilization method; e.g. adsorption of lipid-linked glycans to nitrocellulose, or neoglycoprotein conjugates to polystyrene, nitrocellulose, etc. Describe any specific handling of the glycan derivatives required prior to sample deposition, e.g. formulation by adding carrier reagents. Describe the chemistry on the slide surface that enables the covalent immobilization of the glycan samples; e.g. NHS-ester or epoxide for amine functional groups, maleimide for sulfhydryl functional group.

principles.principle: Provide details of the arrayer/printer and printing parameters (description of arrayer, dispensing mechanism, deposition amounts, printing conditions and environmental conditions).
principles.evidence: We have identified 8 areas, numbered in the workflow shown below, that are required for generating an unambiguous glycan array in the first instance and obtaining binding data. For each numbered component of the workflow area we provide guidelines for the minimal information that should be provided in reporting results.

principles.principle: Describe array layout and provide a map of printed probes (subarray/pad layout, replicate scheme) and report glycan identification and quality control procedures.
principles.evidence: Each array slide contained 16-pad subarrays. Each pad was set up for printing 64 probes maximum, each at 2 levels in duplicate (four spots for one probe in a row); up to 256 spots (16x16) in total in each pad. The 866 lipid-linked probes in the screening arrays were printed on multiple subarrays for parallel binding analyses. The quality control of the screening microarrays of sequence-defined glycan probes was carried out with a collection of biotinylated plant lectins ... These data will be described elsewhere and are available upon request.

principles.principle: Record and report detector/scanner hardware and settings, image analysis software, and data processing methods including normalization or transformation applied to quantified spot data.
principles.evidence: Scanning hardware GenePix 4300A (Molecular Devices, UK) ... Scanner settings: Scanning resolution: 10 μm / pixel; Laser channel: Red (scan wavelength 635 nm); PMT: 350. Image analysis: GenePix® Pro 7 (Molecular Devices). The gpr files were entered into an in-house microarray database ... No particular Data normalization method or statistical analysis was used for the results of the screening arrays. Data were transformed into z-scores by subtracting the mean value across the array and dividing the results by the standard deviation.

principles.principle: Present processed (Level 3) data in publications and retain Level 1 (raw images) and Level 2 (quantified numerical output) data for future access and re-analysis.
principles.evidence: Similar to DNA microarray experiment, there are three levels of data relevant to a glycan microarray experiment: Level 1: Raw data (original TIFF image from array scanner) Level 2: Quantified numerical data output file (e.g. proscan or gpr) from scanner software Level 3: Processed data (after association with glycan identities, averaging of replicates with appropriate statistics, data selection procedures, filtering and sorting, etc.) The present MIRAGE guidelines suggest that only ‘Level 3’ data need be presented in published papers but also suggest that ‘Level 1’ and ‘Level 2’ data be retained by researchers so that it be available when suitable databases and processing software become accessible ...

principles.principle: Report how processed data were interpreted and state any conclusions or specificity findings, noting software/algorithms used or not used.
principles.evidence: No software or algorithms were used to interpret processed data. At the assay condition used, the recombinant CMA1 lectin showed binding showed a broad range of binding activities and bound four types of glycan sequences: galactose (Gal)-terminating, GalNAc-terminating, fucose (Fuc)-terminating and chondroitin sulphate (CS) related sequences.

standards.notes: Extracted principles are drawn from the MIRAGE Glycan Microarray Guidelines (doi:10.3762/mirage.3) and accompanying supplementary templates and example documents provided with the guideline package. Templates exist as supplementary material to help filling these reporting items but the core document is guidance-oriented.

standards.name: MIRAGE Liquid Chromatography Analysis Guidelines
standards.abstract: These guidelines cover reporting of liquid chromatography (LC) experiments used primarily in glycomics analyses — describing LC instrumentation, columns, mobile phases, chromatographic run parameters, pre-/post-run procedures, detection systems, fraction collection and data annotation. The document (MIRAGE LC Guidelines, Version 1.0, 1 March 2018, doi:10.3762/mirage.4) is published by the MIRAGE consortium and provides a minimal information checklist to improve reproducibility and enable data reuse by specifying which metadata should be reported for LC experiments and how to describe equipment, experimental conditions and processing steps.

classification.rationale: The source lists explicit, named metadata items (e.g. "Manufacturer", "Model", "Time stamp", "Gradient") with definitions for each item, i.e. a field-level checklist that maps directly to reportable metadata columns rather than pure procedural instructions. This is presented in a tabular/field format in the guideline and therefore should be represented as a Metadata Table.

standards.notes: Extracted fields are those explicitly named and defined in the MIRAGE LC Guidelines excerpt provided (version 1.0, 2018). Types were assigned to best-fit primitive data formats based on the descriptive definitions in the source; where the source did not state a strict machine-readable type, a conservative type (string/free_text/numeric/datetime/reference/enum) was chosen and the verbatim guideline text is provided as evidence for each field.
